Taiwan power suppliers prepare for Nvidia’s 800VDC architecture
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-18
04:40:55 UTC
13:40:55 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan’s major power suppliers are developing products based on Nvidia’s 800VDC architecture as the new power standard moves toward commercial deployment, CTEE reported.
800VDC, or 800-volt direct current, is emerging as a key power standard for next-generation AI data centers. Current AI server power systems typically require electricity from the grid to undergo multiple conversions from alternating current to direct current before reaching individual racks, resulting in energy losses and generating additional heat, according to Business Next and UDN.
Distributing electricity as DC from an earlier stage can reduce the number of conversions and improve power efficiency. More than 80 equipment manufacturers and infrastructure providers are already developing products based on Nvidia’s specifications, indicating that an 800VDC supply chain is gradually taking shape.
Among Taiwan’s suppliers, Delta Electronics has already entered mass production of high-voltage direct current products. Shipments of its ±400VDC and 800VDC systems are scheduled to begin in the third quarter.
Overall volumes are expected to remain limited this year, with ±400VDC products accounting for a larger share through the end of the year. Shipments of 800VDC systems will depend on the rollout of Nvidia’s new platforms and the pace at which major cloud service providers adopt the architecture. More substantial growth is not expected until next year.
Lite-On Technology Corp. is also preparing its 800VDC power racks for the emerging architecture and is currently validating the products. The company has begun sending initial samples to customers and original design manufacturers, as well as conducting internal testing.
A second round of samples and customer integration testing is planned for October. If both certification stages proceed as scheduled, small-scale mass production could begin as early as November.
Lite-On expects to start larger-scale shipments in the first quarter of next year. One of its facilities in Kaohsiung will initially handle validation and production, while a US customer is expected to begin mass production with the products in the second quarter.
Nvidia plans to introduce the architecture in stages. The first phase, an 800VDC power rack compatible with Nvidia’s MGX platform, is scheduled to launch in the second half of this year and can be integrated with existing facilities.
Next year, the company plans to introduce power centers capable of supplying multiple server racks. Its longer-term goal is to develop facility-level DC power modules capable of converting grid electricity directly into 800VDC.

This was reported by Petro Andriushchenko, head of the Center for the Study of Occupation, on his Telegram channel, citing Russian authorities, UNN writes.
Details
According to him, Russian reports said that air defense and electronic warfare forces operated against more than 150 UAVs during the night and morning. The greatest activity was observed in the southeastern part of the Moscow region, particularly in the Ramenskoye direction.
In the Pavlovsky Posad district, a private house burned down in the village of Kuznetsy, while the roof of a high-rise building caught fire in Pavlovsky Posad. In the Bogorodsk district, two houses in the Albatros garden association were damaged, and a guest house burned in Noginsk.
Andriushchenko separately reported a confirmed direct hit by a UAV on a Wildberries warehouse in the Bogorodsk district. A fire broke out at the facility and was later contained. Preliminary reports indicate there were no casualties.
The attack covered several regions
A shopping pavilion burned in Kolomna; a registry office, a store, and a residential building were also damaged. Construction materials caught fire on the grounds of a residential complex in Kotelniki, while cars and an electrical substation were damaged in Elektrostal.
According to Andriushchenko, the Russian side reported the destruction of more than 80 UAVs in seven districts of Rostov region – Bokovsky, Verkhnedonskoy, Kasharsky, Krasnosulinsky, Millerovsky, Chertkovsky, and Sholokhovsky. 19 August 2026•Update: 19 August 2026
South Korean defense firm Hanwha Aerospace Co. has won a contract to deliver K9 self-propelled howitzer prototypes for the US Army's artillery modernization program, Yonhap News Agency reported Wednesday, citing a company statement.
The company's US unit -- Hanwha Defense USA -- was selected to provide prototypes based on the K9 platform for the army's Mobile Tactical Cannon (MTC) program.
The MTC program aims to develop a highly mobile 155 mm artillery system to replace the US Army's aging M777 towed howitzers.
Under the contract, Hanwha will deliver six MTC prototypes with an option for an additional 12 systems and has a cumulative value of up to $262.9 million, said a separate US Army statement.
"Soldiers will use these platforms in a series of operational experiments to assess performance, reliability and supportability in realistic combat conditions," the statement said.
The contract marks the K9 system's first entry into the US defense market, the world's largest.
In April, Hanwha Defense USA signed a three-year lease for an idle facility in Opelika, Alabama as part of efforts to localize production in the US.
The company said it also plans to invest in the US self-propelled howitzer supply chain to expand its presence in the combat vehicle market.
The K9 system is already in service or under contract in a number of countries, including NATO members such as Poland, Romania, Norway and Finland.
